Version 7.1.0

Build software with a focused agent team.

Agent-Team gives one AI agent the lead. The pure orchestrator derives safe parallel work, delegates building and verification, supervises continuously, and joins only verified work.

Important: Agent-Team is a skill for Codex or Claude Code. It is not a shell command. You speak to it inside your AI coding host.

On this page What it doesInstallDependencies InvokeSet upSettings LaunchDashboardMemory and contextHarness logicProject Kickoff

What Agent-Team does

Think about a group science project. One student keeps the plan. Other students work on separate parts. A final student checks the facts. Agent-Team uses the same idea for software work.

Short version:
Plan the work.
Give each agent one clear job.
Review every result.
Join the safe parts.
  • The pure orchestratorOwns scope, task choice, parallel-set derivation, continuous supervision, integration, and release. It does not implement or verify the work itself.
  • The developerBuilds one bounded task in a separate worktree.
  • The delegated verifierRuns pre-dispatch and post-completion verification with GPT-5.6-Sol at medium effort; Claude Code uses an Opus 5 fallback when that route is unavailable.

Agent-Team can use more than one developer when tasks do not touch the same files. The host can reduce the team count when it needs space for review. Only the orchestrator assigns work. Worker agents do not create more worker agents.

Install the complete package

Choose one host and one scope. User scope makes the skill available across projects. Project scope keeps it in one project.

ScopeCodexClaude Code
User~/.agents/skills/agent-team~/.claude/skills/agent-team
Project.agents/skills/agent-team.claude/skills/agent-team

  1. Open a supported host

    Install Codex or Claude Code. Sign in to your own account. Confirm that your account can use the models that you select.

  2. Check the base tools

    Check Git, GitHub CLI, Node.js 24, and npm. Use gh auth status to check GitHub access. Never paste a token into chat.

  3. Ask the agent to install it

    Recommended install prompt
    Install the complete Agent-Team package from https://github.com/thebpandey/agent-team. Use release v7.1.0 and my authorized GitHub access. Inspect the source, license, exact revision, and any existing installation first. Preserve custom files and unrelated settings. Use this actual host only. Use user scope unless I name a project scope. Verify the package and tell me which reload or trust steps remain.

  4. Reload and review trust

    Restart or reload the host. Review its hook list. In Codex, use /hooks when that control is available. Trust only the entries that you reviewed.

Installer reference for maintainers

Run the bundled helper from the checked Agent-Team package. Choose one command.

Codex, user scope
node hooks/agent-team-cli.mjs install --host codex --scope user
Claude Code, project scope
node hooks/agent-team-cli.mjs install --host claude-code --scope project --project /absolute/project/root

Know the dependencies

A dependency is a tool that Agent-Team uses. Setup checks whether each selected tool works. A file on disk is not enough.

Required

  • Codex or Claude Code: runs the skill and the agents.
  • Git: tracks changes and supports separate worktrees.
  • Node.js 24 and npm: run Agent-Team helpers and hooks.
  • Serena: helps agents find and understand exact symbols and code.
  • Graphify: works beside Serena, producing a code-only repository graph for blast radius, paths, and hotspots.
  • Microsoft Playwright CLI: checks real browser behavior. It is required even for backend projects.
  • Python and uv: support Serena when the selected release needs them.

Default or optional

  • Default profiles: ast-grep, narrowed LeanCTX, Superpowers, Ponytail, Impeccable, and React Best Practices. LeanCTX uses shell_security = "warn": interpreter one-liners warn visibly but never grant permission.
  • Beads: an optional task tracker. A root or designated TASKS.md file also works.
  • Context7: optional current library documentation.
  • beads_viewer: optional dashboard for a selected Beads graph.
  • subagent-tax: optional maintainer diagnostic. It is not an onboarding tool.
First-use rule: Setup prepares missing required tools and selected defaults. Optional tools stay off until you select them. Sign-in, payment, administrator approval, and native hook trust still belong to you.

Set up the project

Setup prepares the project. It does not start development or turn on deployment.

  1. Confirm the project root

    Agent-Team finds the main Git project, its integration branch, and the selected task tracker.

  2. Give it ready work

    Use an approved Project Kickoff handoff, an existing plan, or one clear task with acceptance checks.

  3. Run setup

    Codex
    $agent-team setup
    Claude Code
    /agent-team setup

  4. Read the readiness report

    Look for four groups: host access, runtimes and tools, selected skills, and project readiness. Fix each item marked Missing, Manual action, or Unavailable.

  5. Complete your manual steps

    Finish sign-in, organization access, administrator approval, host reload, and hook trust when setup requests them.

Choose settings

Settings belong to the project. Codex and Claude Code keep separate model choices. A saved choice cannot change the model of the current parent session.

Show the compact settings view
$agent-team settings
Change one setting in plain language
Agent-Team, change only the reviewer model. Show supported choices, effort levels, cost trade-offs, and the current recommendation.
Run settingBuilt-in valueMeaning
parallel_teams1Requested active development teams. The supported range is 1 to 6.
continuousfalseWhen on, the orchestrator continuously derives the next authorized parallel set after verified integration or safe parking frees capacity.
auto_deployfalseWhen on, release verified batches to an already authorized target.
deploy_batch_tasksNot setUse the effective run limit unless you select a task batch size.

A start command can override these values for one run. It does not change the saved defaults.

Launch a run

Start only after setup reports enough readiness for the selected work.

One ready task

Codex
$agent-team start

Two teams with refill

Codex
$agent-team start 2 continuous

One named task

Codex
$agent-team start email-preferences

Require a preview

Claude Code
/agent-team start with-preview
Team count is not agent count. The pure orchestrator derives a parallel set only from authorized tasks with no unmet dependencies and disjoint writable paths. Each task can need a developer and a delegated verifier, so host limits can reduce the number of tasks that run at the same time.

Every pre-dispatch check and post-completion verification goes to the delegated GPT-5.6-Sol verifier at medium effort. In Claude Code, Opus 5 is the fallback route. The orchestrator keeps supervising worker progress and routes ordinary findings back for repair instead of pausing for a new prompt.

Pause, resume, and check status
Read recorded status
$agent-team status all
Pause after safe checkpoints
$agent-team pause all
Resume from saved evidence
$agent-team resume all

Inspect the optional local dashboard

The dashboard is a local, read-only view of the selected tracker. It is never a second task authority or a background controller.

Snapshot by default

Ask for a local dashboard snapshot to see task progress, teams, freshness, and recorded evidence. Reload the generated HTML after a new snapshot; a browser reload cannot refresh the tracker on its own.

Live mode is opt-in

A small local process may refresh the same status model on loopback only. Stop it when finished. It does not admit work, change task state, or replace the orchestrator.

Generate a local snapshot
node hooks/agent-team-cli.mjs dashboard-snapshot --project /absolute/project/root

If data is unavailable, retain the last usable snapshot and label it stale or unavailable; never show unavailable data as complete.

How Agent-Team keeps memory and context under control

An AI agent has limited working space. Agent-Team keeps that space useful. It sends each worker the facts needed for one task and stores durable facts in the correct project record.

Small task packets

Each worker gets one bounded packet. It names the task ID, acceptance checks, owned paths, source revision, relevant rules, evidence location, and next action. The worker does not receive the full conversation or every installed skill.

One source of truth

The selected Tracker owns task state. Project documents own approved decisions. A checkpoint points to those records; it does not become a second task tracker.

Relevant reading

A fresh worker reads the complete instructions that apply to its job, plus the exact source and tests it needs. A retained worker reuses context that is still valid. No worker treats another agent's summary as proof.

Bounded checkpoints

Before a handoff, pause, or compaction, the agent updates CONTEXT.md. It stays under 600 words in normal use and records the owner, revision, evidence, pending operations, and next action.

Where durable information lives

InformationAuthoritative homeWhy
Task status and dependenciesTrackerEvery agent reads the same work state.
Approved product and technical decisionsProject documentsDecisions survive handoffs without copying the full chat.
Current attempt and recovery pointersCONTEXT.mdA replacement agent can verify the correct owner, worktree, revision, and next action.
Reusable lessons and failed approachesMISTAKES.mdThe team can avoid repeating a known problem.
Exact implementation and test evidenceGit and saved evidenceSummaries never replace the real source or test output.
Compact output, exact recovery. LeanCTX can reduce routine source and shell output while keeping the original available for recovery. Its narrowed profile uses shell_security = "warn", so interpreter one-liners are logged warnings rather than permission bypasses. It is a helper only. It does not become a second task tracker, and cached input does not make the context window larger. Native auto-compaction stays enabled as a fallback.

How the harness works

  1. Read ready work. The orchestrator reads the one selected tracker.
  2. Derive the parallel set. It checks scope, dependencies, ownership, branch, acceptance, and disjoint writable paths before claiming only safe work.
  3. Claim each task. A claim prevents two writers from owning the same work.
  4. Build in isolation. A developer uses a separate Git worktree and owns only named paths.
  5. Verify independently. GPT-5.6-Sol at medium effort checks pre-dispatch and completed revisions; Claude Code uses an Opus 5 fallback.
  6. Repair problems. Normal findings return to the developer. The pure orchestrator supervises continuously and the verifier checks the repair again.
  7. Integrate verified work. The orchestrator joins the safe revision into the chosen integration branch.
  8. Continue or stop. Continuous mode derives the next authorized parallel set. A finite run reports its result.
  9. Release separately. Deployment needs an authorized target and all required gates.
If work is blocked: Agent-Team saves a safe checkpoint, keeps the task claim, and frees stopped compute when it can. Resume checks ownership and current evidence before work continues.

Use Project Kickoff first

Project Kickoff is optional. It helps you decide what to build. Agent-Team then helps you build the approved plan.

Project Kickoff

Moves through discovery, approved planning, setup, and handoff. It asks one unresolved question at a time. It creates the approved product, experience, technical, scaffold, and handoff records. It does not implement product features.

Agent-Team

Reuses the approved handoff. It loads the task tracker, checks readiness, assigns bounded work, reviews changes, integrates verified revisions, and releases only with authority.

  1. Install Project Kickoff

    Use the official Project Kickoff repository. Install the complete package in the matching project skill folder. Follow its license. Keep a private package out of application commits.

  2. Start or audit the project

    New project in Codex
    $project-kickoff start Build a study planner for high-school students.
    Existing project in Claude Code
    /project-kickoff audit /absolute/path/to/project

  3. Answer one question at a time

    Approve each planning stage. Project Kickoff records the decisions. A changed decision updates only the affected plans.

  4. Complete the handoff

    Approve PLAN.md, choose one tracker, and let Project Kickoff seed stable task IDs. It prepares Agent-Team but does not start it.

  5. Set up Agent-Team

    Reuse the handoff
    $agent-team setup
Reuse the approved Project Kickoff handoff and its selected tracker. Preserve the integration branch, task IDs, acceptance checks, and recorded decisions.

  6. Launch the approved work

    Safe first run
    $agent-team start
Example in plain language

You ask Project Kickoff to plan a study app. It helps you choose users, features, design, technology, and tests. It writes an approved plan and creates the task records. You then ask Agent-Team to set up. Agent-Team reads those records. It gives the login task to one developer and the schedule task to another when their files do not conflict. A reviewer checks each result. The orchestrator integrates only work that passes.

If you already have a good plan and tracker, you can skip Project Kickoff. Agent-Team does not require it.
